gloss: touch; reach, come to; strike; a stroke, plague, mark of skin disease
summary: To touch, and from touching, to reach and to strike. The qal is to lay a hand on or come into contact with: the tree in the garden, the holy mountain, the altar, a carcass or the dead, a woman, and, of Yahweh or his messenger, the touch that strengthens or that harms; it is also to reach as far as (the sword to the life, judgment to the heavens). The hiphil makes something touch (the coal to Isaiah's lips, Yahweh's hand to Jeremiah's mouth), brings down to the dust, and is to reach or arrive, of a time, a day, a turn; the piel is Yahweh striking with a plague, and the passive participle is the one “stricken” (Isa 53:4). The noun נֶגַע is the stroke itself: a blow or plague sent by Yahweh, and above all the mark of skin disease that the priest inspected on a man, a garment or a house (Lev 13–14).

words.gloss: touch; reach, arrive; strike; (hiphil) make touch, bring down to
words.summary: About 150 times. Touch is the root of every use: what touches reaches, and what touches with force strikes. Under the law touch carries holiness and uncleanness (Exo 29:37; Lev 5:2–3; Hag 2:12–13), so “do not touch” guards both the holy and the clean. The brief's two verb tokens with no stem (Lev 13:29; Deu 21:5) are the noun נֶגַע in pause, filed here by spelling; the noun's six “qal” tokens are this verb.

stems.gloss: touch; harm; reach as far as; (passive participle) stricken

senses.definition: To come into contact with, by hand or body: the forbidden tree, the holy mountain, the altar and holy things, the unclean and the dead; also of a man with a woman. Touch passes uncleanness, and from the altar holiness.

evidence.note: “You shall not eat of it and you shall not touch it (וְלֹא תִגְּעוּ בּוֹ), lest you die.”
“Take heed not to go up into the mountain or touch its edge; whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.”
“No hand shall touch him”: he is stoned or shot, not handled.
“Whatever touches the altar shall be holy.”
“Everything that touches them shall be holy.”
A נֶפֶשׁ that touches any unclean thing, a carcass or the uncleanness of man, is unclean and guilty.
“Of their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcass you shall not touch.”
“He who touches the flesh of the one with a flow shall wash his clothes … and be unclean until evening.”
The sons of Kohath “shall not touch the holy thing, lest they die”.
“He who touches the dead, any נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם, shall be unclean seven days.”
One slain by the sword, or a dead man, or a human bone, or a grave.
Holy flesh carried in a fold of the garment does not make bread holy by touching it; one unclean by a dead נֶפֶשׁ who touches it makes it unclean.
“Depart, depart, go out from there, touch no unclean thing”: quoted in 2Co 6:17.
Defiled with blood, “they could not touch their garments … Depart! Unclean! Depart, depart, do not touch!”
The dead man let down into Elisha's grave “touched the bones of Elisha, and he lived and stood on his feet”.
The cherubs' wings touched the one wall, the other wall, and each other.
Esther drew near and touched the top of the sceptre.
The male goat came over the face of all the earth “and was not touching the earth”.

senses.definition: Of a man with a woman, to have relations with her, or to lay a hand on her at all.

evidence.note: God to Abimelech: “I kept you from sinning against me; therefore I did not let you touch her.”
“So is he who goes in to his neighbour's wife; whoever touches her shall not go unpunished.”
Boaz has charged the young men not to touch Ruth.

senses.gloss: touch, of Yahweh or his messenger
senses.definition: The touch of Yahweh or of his messenger: to wake, strengthen and commission, or to move the heart; on the earth and the mountains, a touch that melts and makes them smoke.

evidence.note: “A messenger touched him and said, Arise, eat”; again in 1Ki 19:7.
“One having the appearance of a man touched me again and strengthened me (וַיְחַזְּקֵנִי).”
“One like the sons of man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and spoke.”
Gabriel “touched me (or reached me) about the time of the evening offering”.
“Behold, this has touched your lips, and your iniquity is taken away and your sin covered.”
“The men of valour whose hearts God had touched” went with Saul.
The messenger of Yahweh touched the flesh and the cakes with the tip of his staff, and fire consumed them.
“Yahweh of Armies, who touches the land and it melts.”
“He touches the mountains and they smoke.”

senses.definition: To lay a hand on someone to hurt him, or of a disaster or a blow, to strike.

evidence.note: “He who touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.”
“As we have not touched you, and as we have done to you only good.”
“We have sworn to them by Yahweh … so now we may not touch them.”
“Do not touch my anointed ones, and do my prophets no harm (אַל־תָּרֵעוּ).”
“He who touches you touches the apple of his eye.”
“He shall not touch you any more.”
The adversary: “Put out your hand and touch all that he has, and he will bless you to your face”.
“Touch his bone and his flesh.”
“The hand of God has touched me.”
“It touches you and you are dismayed.”
“In seven, evil shall not touch you.”
If the cart does not go to Beth-shemesh, “we shall know that it is not his hand that struck us”.
A great wind “struck the four corners of the house”.
“When the east wind touches it, it will wither.”
“He touched the socket of his hip, and the socket of Jacob's hip was put out of joint.”
“They did not know that evil was touching them”; again in Jdg 20:41.

senses.definition: To reach as far as, of a spreading vine, a sword, a judgment or a disaster; and to come to, of a word or a time.

evidence.note: “The sword has reached to the נֶפֶשׁ (עַד־הַנָּפֶשׁ).”
“This is your evil, for it is bitter, for it has reached to your heart.”
“Her judgment has reached to the heavens and is lifted up to the clouds.”
“It has come to Judah; it has reached to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.”
The vine of Sibmah: “they reached to Jazer”.
“The word reached the king of Nineveh.”
“When the seventh month came (וַיִּגַּע).”
“Bloodshed touches bloodshed”: one follows hard upon another.
“The man who touches them (the thorns) arms himself with iron.”
“Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him reach (וְיִגַּע) the water shaft.”

senses.definition: The passive participle נָגוּעַ: struck by God with a stroke, the plight of the leper; said of the servant of Yahweh.

evidence.note: “We esteemed him stricken (נָגוּעַ), smitten of God (מֻכֵּה אֱלֹהִים) and afflicted.”
“I have been stricken all the day, and my rebuke comes every morning.”

stems.gloss: let oneself be struck, feign defeat

senses.gloss: be struck, make as if beaten
senses.definition: Once, of Joshua's army at Ai drawing the enemy out by the planned flight: to let oneself be struck before the enemy.

evidence.note: “Joshua and all Israel were struck (וַיִּנָּגְעוּ) before them and fled by the way of the wilderness”, as planned in Jos 8:5–6.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh, to strike a man and his house with plagues, or a king with skin disease.

evidence.note: “Yahweh struck (וַיְנַגַּע) Pharaoh and his house with great plagues (נְגָעִים) because of Sarai.”
“Yahweh struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death.”
Uzziah with skin disease on his forehead, “for Yahweh had struck him”.

senses.definition: Once, of the wicked who prosper: they are not stricken as other men are.

evidence.note: “They are not in the trouble of man, and with mankind they are not stricken (יְנֻגָּעוּ).”

stems.gloss: make touch, apply; bring down to; reach, arrive, come

senses.definition: To bring one thing into contact with another: the blood to the doorposts, the foreskin to the feet, the coal to the lips, Yahweh's hand to the prophet's mouth; house joined to house.

evidence.note: “Dip it in the blood … and touch (וְהִגַּעְתֶּם) the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood.”
Zipporah cut off her son's foreskin “and made it touch his feet”.
“He made it touch my mouth and said, Behold, this has touched your lips.”
“Yahweh put out his hand and touched my mouth, and Yahweh said to me, Behold, I have put my words in your mouth.”
“Woe to those who join (מַגִּיעֵי) house to house, who add field to field.”

senses.definition: To bring a wall or a city down until it touches the dust.

evidence.note: “The lofty city he lays low, lays it low to the earth, makes it touch the dust.”
“He will bring down, lay low, bring to the ground, to the dust.”
“He has brought down to the ground in dishonour the kingdom and its princes.”

senses.definition: To reach as far as, of a ladder, a wing, a flood, a valley, a means; to draw near, of a life to the grave and death; and to arrive, of a time, a day, a turn, a decree, or a person.

evidence.note: “A ladder set up on the earth, and its top reaching (מַגִּיעַ) to the heavens.”
The cherubs' wings reaching the wall of the house and each other.
The river of Assyria “shall reach to the neck”.
“The valley of the mountains shall reach to Azal.”
“In a flood of great waters they shall not reach him.”
“Though his head reach to the clouds.”
“A rage that has reached to the heavens.”
“If his hand cannot reach (לֹא תַגִּיעַ יָדוֹ) the sufficiency of a lamb”: cannot afford.
“My life has drawn near (הִגִּיעוּ) to the grave (לִשְׁאוֹל).”
“They drew near to the gates of death.”
“The time has come, the day has arrived (הִגִּיעַ).”
“The time of singing has come.”
“Before the evil days come and the years draw near.”
Righteous men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked.
“When the turn of Esther … came to go in to the king.”
Wherever the king's word and decree came.
“Who knows whether you have come (הִגַּעַתְּ) to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
“Wait until we come to you.”
The goat came close beside the ram.
“Blessed is he who waits and reaches (וְיַגִּיעַ) the thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.”

evidence.locator: Gen.3.3, תִגְּעוּ → ἅψησθε; Isa.52.11, תִּגָּעוּ → ἅπτεσθε; Psa.105.15 → ἅπτεσθε; Isa.6.7; Jer.1.9 → ἥψατο; Zec.2.12 → ἁπτόμενος; ἅπτομαι renders נָגַע ×80

evidence.note: “Come out from their midst and be separate, says the Lord, and touch (ἅπτεσθε) no unclean thing”: Isa 52:11.
Jesus “stretched out his hand and touched (ἥψατο) him”, the leper, and he was cleansed: the touch that under the law defiled (Lev 5:3) here makes clean.
He touched the bier of the dead young man and raised him, as the dead man who touched Elisha's bones lived (2Ki 13:21).
“Do not handle (ἅψῃ), do not taste, do not touch (θίγῃς)”: ordinances of men, set aside.
“If even a beast touches (θίγῃ) the mountain, it shall be stoned”: Exo 19:12–13.

evidence.locator: Psa.88.4, הִגִּיעוּ → ἤγγισεν; Psa.107.18 → ἤγγισαν; Jer.51.9; Jon.3.6 → ἤγγισεν

evidence.note: “Behold, the hour has drawn near (ἤγγικεν)”: the time that arrives, as Ezk 7:12.
“The night is far spent, the day has drawn near (ἤγγικεν).”
“Then the kingdom of God has come (ἔφθασεν) upon you.”
“We came (ἐφθάσαμεν) even as far as you”: reach.

parallels.note: “Do harm”: touch not, do no harm.
“Draw near”: the hiphil's arriving, of a life near the grave and death.

phrases.gloss: bring down to the ground, to the dust

words.gloss: stroke, blow, plague; mark of skin disease
words.summary: About 78 times, more than fifty of them in Lev 13–14. The stroke is what touches and strikes: a blow between men, a plague sent by Yahweh, and the mark the priest inspected for skin disease (צָרַעַת) on a body, a garment or the wall of a house.

senses.definition: A blow or plague that strikes, sent by Yahweh on a house, a land or a man, or a son's chastening; the trouble a man knows in his own heart.

evidence.note: “Yahweh struck (וַיְנַגַּע) Pharaoh and his house with great plagues (נְגָעִים).”
“One more plague (נֶגַע אֶחָד) I will bring on Pharaoh and on Egypt”: the death of the firstborn.
Of David's son: “I will be to him a father and he shall be to me a son; when he commits iniquity I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the strokes (וּבְנִגְעֵי) of the sons of man.”
“I will visit their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with strokes (וּבִנְגָעִים).”
“Remove your stroke from me; I am consumed by the blow of your hand.”
“No evil shall befall you, and no plague come near your tent.”
“My loved ones and my friends stand aloof from my plague.”
“Whatever plague, whatever sickness … each knowing the plague of his own heart (נֶגַע לְבָבוֹ).”
“He was cut off from the land of the living; for the transgression of my people the stroke was his (נֶגַע לָמוֹ).”
The adulterer: “a stroke and dishonour he will find, and his reproach will not be wiped away”.

senses.definition: In the law of cases brought to judgment: a stroke one man gives another, a case of assault.

evidence.note: “Between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke (בֵּין נֶגַע לָנֶגַע).”
By the word of the priests “shall every dispute and every stroke be settled”.

senses.definition: The mark of skin disease, צָרַעַת, that the priest examined and pronounced clean or unclean: on the skin of a man or woman, on a garment or leather, on the walls of a house.

evidence.note: “When a man has on the skin of his flesh a swelling or a scab or a bright spot, and it becomes on the skin of his flesh a נֶגַע צָרַעַת, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest … and the priest shall see the mark.”
The one in whom the mark is: torn clothes, “Unclean, unclean!”, dwelling alone outside the camp.
“A garment in which is the mark of skin disease”, wool or linen or leather.
“I put the mark of skin disease in a house of the land of your possession … Something like a mark has appeared to me in the house.”
“This is the law for every mark of skin disease.”
“Take heed in the mark of skin disease to do all that the priests the Levites teach you.”
“Seven messengers having seven plagues (πληγάς), the last”: plagues after the pattern of those on Egypt (Exo 11:1).
“As many as had plagues (μάστιγας) pressed upon him to touch (ἅψωνται) him”: the noun and the verb together.
The woman with a flow of blood touched his garment and “knew in her body that she was healed of the plague (μάστιγος)”.

parallels.note: “Rod”: the rod and the strokes of chastening.

cognates.gloss: touch; (aphel) bring into contact; (pael) afflict with skin disease; (ithpaal) be stricken with skin disease
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in the Targums and Talmud: touch, and the stroke of skin disease, the same two sides as the Hebrew verb and noun. The Targum of Isa 6:1 says Uzziah was stricken (ithpaal) with it, as 2Ki 15:5 has the piel. The Talmudic uses may owe something to Mishnaic Hebrew.

evidence.locator: s.v. נְגַע (ch.), citing Snh. 19a (לְמִינְגַּע, touch the corpse); Bekh. 28b (Af., make touch); Ḥull. 60a (Pa. part. pass. מְנַגַּע, one stricken with leprosy); Targ. Is. VI, 1 (Ithpa.)

cognates.gloss: (of words, medicine, fodder) enter into one and take effect; (VIII) go in search of pasture
cognates.note: The consonants answer (Arabic j for Hebrew g), but the sense is a word or remedy that reaches into a man and takes effect, not touch. It comes near only the qal “reach as far as” (the sword reaching to the נֶפֶשׁ, Jer 4:10), where it is named as possible.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 3028, art. نجع, نَجَعَ فِيهِ (n43831)
evidence.note: “It (a discourse, and exhortation; and medicine; and fodder) entered into him, and produced an effect upon him.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 3028, art. نجع, اِنْتَجَعَ (n43832)
evidence.note: “He sought after herbage in its place.”

doctrine.statement: The law of the red heifer says “he who touches the dead, any נֶפֶשׁ of man (לְכָל־נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם), shall be unclean seven days”, and “whoever touches the dead, the נֶפֶשׁ of the man who dies (בְּנֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר־יָמוּת)” and does not purify himself defiles the tabernacle of Yahweh (Num 19:11, 13). What lies there to be touched is the נֶפֶשׁ, and it is the נֶפֶשׁ that dies. Haggai's question is put in the same words: one “unclean by a נֶפֶשׁ” who touches food makes it unclean (Hag 2:13). The law knows no part of the man that goes on living when he dies; it knows the dead body, the living soul that has died, and it counts death the deepest uncleanness. The first “do not touch” carried the same warning: “lest you die” (Gen 3:3; 2:17), and to dust he returned (Gen 3:19).

When a dead man was thrown into Elisha's grave, “the man went down and touched the bones of Elisha, and he lived and stood on his feet” (2Ki 13:21). Life came back to the body, and he stood up: a raising of the dead man himself, by the power of Yahweh at work through his prophet. Jesus likewise touched the bier and said, “Young man, I say to you, arise”, and the dead man sat up and spoke (Luk 7:14–15). These are pledges of the resurrection at his return, when those in the graves will hear his voice and come out (Joh 5:28–29), the dead in Christ rising when he descends from heaven (1Th 4:16).

Of the servant of Yahweh Isaiah says, “we esteemed him stricken (נָגוּעַ), smitten of God and afflicted”, the word used of one struck with skin disease (2Ki 15:5; 2Ch 26:20); yet “he was pierced for our transgressions … for the transgression of my people the stroke (נֶגַע) was his” (Isa 53:4–5, 8). Philip began from this scripture and preached Jesus (Act 8:32–35), and Matthew and Peter apply the chapter to him (Mat 8:17; 1Pe 2:24). The one stricken was a man who was cut off out of the land of the living (Isa 53:8), and God raised him: Yahweh “shall prolong his days” (Isa 53:10). The same strokes are promised to David's son, “I will be to him a father and he shall be to me a son … I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the strokes of the sons of man” (2Sa 7:14); Hebrews applies the first words to Jesus (Heb 1:5). He is God's son, begotten as David's seed (2Sa 7:12; Luk 1:32–35), bearing the strokes of the sons of man in their nature.

note: Draft from the brief. No proper names are formed from the root (none in TIPNR), and no word of it sat in another entry. BDB's n.aw.aa and n.aw.ab cross-file six tokens by spelling: the verb's two no-stem tokens (Lev 13:29; Deu 21:5) are the noun in pause, and the noun's six qal tokens are the verb; the counts in `lexicon-support` include them twice. Isa 53:4 and Psa 73:14 נָגוּעַ are filed under the qal (passive participle). The niphal of Jos 8:15 is read with Jos 8:5–6 as a planned, feigned defeat; the text itself says only “were struck”. Cognates: the Peshitta has no ܢܓܥ (SEDRA lists no NGE root), so the only certain cognate is Jewish Aramaic, which may be shaped by Mishnaic Hebrew; Ugaritic, Akkadian (Oracc's ng- words are unrelated) and Ge'ez not found. Arabic نجع “take effect on” is kept as possible only; if a better Arabic or Ge'ez cognate turns up (Dillmann and Leslau not consulted), it would settle the sound behind ע. Open: whether Dan 9:21 is “touched me” or “reached me”; whether the noun's “stroke” and the skin-disease mark should be one sense.
